- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or adjust downward if sentiment shifts to neutral/negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast slope; mean-revert toward recent 7-day average if sentiment remains negative.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates true volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–15% for 30-day horizon.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early 30d (e.g., first 5–7 days), apply downward bias correction of 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment is positive but price action shows mean reversion (e.g., 3 consecutive days below 50% of 30d avg), reduce forecast by 3–5% per day to avoid over-leverage.
